rationale: r2gaussian-claude-agentic: val_n=214, gs_n_gaussians=256, gs_n_iter=150, gs_lr_pos=0.005, gs_lr_scale=0.01, gs_lr_amp=0.01, gs_lr_rot=0.01, gs_amp_init=0.01, gs_scale_init=0.04, gs_tv_weight=0.0001, gs_n_clip=0.05, gs_init_from_fbp=False, gs_outer_wall_s=1080, rationale=iter-5 (search-20260619-01). ONE KNOB: gs_n_gaussians 512->256 (per-scene Gaussian COUNT, from iter-1 BEST base: n_iter=150 / all other knobs held). FAILURE MODE established iters 1-4: r2gaussian is a PER-SCENE Gaussian-splatting fit (no training/amortization) and is BUDGET-INCOMPATIBLE with the 214-slice Mayo protocol at the hard 20-min wall. The gs_n_iter axis is fully mapped and its optimum is iter-1 (n_iter=150, 26/214 scenes, SSIM 0.7383, BEST). BOTH gs_n_iter levers REFUTED in numbers: QUALITY (iter-2 150->400 steps = -0.0001 FLAT) and COVERAGE-via-fewer-steps (iter-3 26->64 scenes = -0.057 DESTRUCTIVE, because a 60-step per-scene Gaussian recon scores BELOW the 0.808 LD-FBP init it replaces). gs_n_iter cannot decouple coverage from quality (cutting steps cuts quality). gs_n_gaussians is the UNTRIED axis that attacks the binding limiter (per-scene step COST = 0.282 s/step at 512 Gaussians, dominated by the dense rasterization + one 2304-view forward/back-proj) WITHOUT touching the 150-step per-scene budget that produced the BEST result. HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable in NUMBERS): halving the Gaussian count halves the per-step rasterization cost (~0.282->~0.16 s/step) so at n_iter=150 per-scene ~24 s -> 1080s wall / 24 = ~45/214 scenes (~1.7x iter-1 coverage) at the SAME 150-step quality. If a 256-Gaussian / 150-step per-scene recon is AT/ABOVE its FBP init, ~doubled coverage LIFTS the 214-avg above iter-1 best 0.7383; if it is BELOW FBP (like iter-3 60-step recons), more coverage HURTS toward iter-3 0.681. FALSIFIER: if SSIM <= 0.7383 (no lift over iter-1 best), the coverage-at-fixed-150-step-quality axis is exhausted -> r2gaussian is STRUCTURALLY budget-incompatible with the 214-slice Mayo protocol (documented NEGATIVE RESULT, hr 0): no (gs_n_iter, gs_n_gaussians) both covers all 214 AND fits any scene above its FBP init in 20 min. PREDICTION: SSIM ~0.68-0.73, hr 0 (the 150-step per-scene Gaussian recon is itself sub-FBP, so doubling coverage of sub-FBP recons most likely DROPS the avg toward 0.681 -- the structural ceiling). BUDGET MATH: ~24 s/scene x 45 scenes = ~1080s ~ the gs_outer_wall_s=1080 in-solver wall (self-truncates, scores whatever completed, exactly as iters 1-4); SLURM --time=00:30:00 default has headroom (~1100-1140s observed elapsed_s, val figure excluded). val_n stays 214 (NOT reduced) per mandate; gs_n_gaussians 256 well within the <=1024 cap. TRAJECTORY: iter-2 0.7370 (10/214) -> iter-1 0.7383 (26/214, BEST, 512 Gaussians) -> iter-3 0.6810 (64/214) | iter-5 = ~45/214 at 256 Gaussians, the coverage-at-fixed-quality test of the structural-ceiling verdict.
